_README: WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. phase10_ablations.py refuses to LAUNCH an arm when any
file in MODEL_SOURCES (more/model.py, more/engine.py, more/data.py) is newer
than the oldest reused T9.1 baseline run, or when its sha256 has drifted from
phase10_code_fingerprint.json. That guard is the T10.H lesson and must not be
weakened. On 2026-08-29 it refused the fixed_depth seeds 45-46 extension, and
the refusal was a FALSE POSITIVE: the only changed file was more/engine.py, and
the only change was T11.1 audit item 7, which added validation-pass depth
accumulation INSIDE `with torch.no_grad()` in the eval loop (engine.py:666-784).
That code reduces tensors the forward pass already returned, consumes no RNG,
and touches no parameter or optimizer state -- so it cannot alter training.
The guard was NOT edited and the fingerprint was NOT re-pinned. Instead the
claim the guard exists to protect was proved directly, and seeds 45-46 were
launched with the exact command launch() builds. Aggregation still runs through
the driver (--report-only), so one_field_check and the resolution-floor warning
were not bypassed -- only the mtime/hash precondition on launching was.
READ THIS BEFORE launching any further Phase 10 arm: the guard will still
refuse, and it should, until someone re-establishes comparability the same way.

more/engine.py.change: T11.1 audit item 7 -- val/* depth accumulation in the validation loop
more/engine.py.training_effect: none; inside torch.no_grad() in model.eval(), pure reductions over already-returned tensors

method: Re-ran the fixed_depth arm config at seed 42 for ONE epoch on the current
epoch-1 quantity in results.tsv against the recorded 50-epoch run
t10_more_fixed_depth_seed42__5bcde9fd, which was trained by the pre-T11.1
engine.py. Epoch 1 is independent of the total epoch count for this arm: the
CosineAnnealingLR scheduler steps only AFTER epoch 1, and the halt-loss
warmup (0.2 * total_steps) scales a ponder cost that fixed_depth does not
produce. The exact match below confirms both facts at once -- had either the
training computation or the warmup interaction differed, train_task_loss
averaged over 59,500 records would not agree to 6 decimal places.

val_loss: The recorded run's epoch-1 val_loss is N/A: logging.log_interval = 2 gates
validation on `epoch % 2 == 0 or epoch == epochs`, so a 50-epoch run does
not validate at epoch 1 while a 1-epoch run does (1 == epochs). Nothing to
compare, and the difference is in the LOGGING gate, not the computation.

reproduction_proof.verdict: training computation unchanged; seeds 42-46 of the fixed_depth arm share one code state

why: fixed_depth was the one Phase 10 arm whose verdict could still change with
more seeds: at n=3 it sat at p = 0.125 with d = -1.90 (BETTER than canonical
MoRE) and a resolution floor of 0.0179, so it could not reach the Bonferroni
threshold alpha = 0.05/6 = 0.0083 no matter how large the effect. At 5-vs-5
the floor drops to 0.0040. The other three n=3 arms (router_noise p = 0.411,
two_blocks p = 0.750, ponder_cost_low p = 0.161) are nowhere near the floor,
so seeds would not change their verdicts and were not spent.
